# DMN TCK report

<!-- Generated by `npm run tck:report`. Do not edit by hand. -->

Measured against the [DMN TCK](https://github.com/dmn-tck/tck), which is the
only independent measure of DMN conformance there is. Every number here comes
from a run of the suite; nothing is estimated and nothing is excluded.

This is **not** a claim of a DMN conformance level. Conformance levels are
defined by the OMG specification, not by a test pass rate, and this runtime
does not claim one.

## Results

| Scope | Passing | Total | |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Level 2 | 122 | 126 | 96.8% |
| Level 3 | 2269 | 3369 | 67.3% |
| **Overall** | **2391** | **3495** | **68.4%** |

## Compliance level 2

4 failing assertions, listed in full:

| Test | Category | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| `0008-LX-arithmetic/0008-LX-arithmetic-test-01/002/payment` | VALUE_MISMATCH | expected 562.707359373292, got 562.7073593732659271562143285576524 (562.707359373266 at the 15 significant digits recorded) |
| `0008-LX-arithmetic/0008-LX-arithmetic-test-01/003/payment` | VALUE_MISMATCH | expected 2861.03377700389, got 2861.033777003901636716262779605767 (2861.0337770039 at the 15 significant digits recorded) |
| `0009-invocation-arithmetic/0009-invocation-arithmetic-test-01/002/MonthlyPayment` | VALUE_MISMATCH | expected 662.707359373292, got 662.7073593732659271562143285576524 (662.707359373266 at the 15 significant digits recorded) |
| `0009-invocation-arithmetic/0009-invocation-arithmetic-test-01/003/MonthlyPayment` | VALUE_MISMATCH | expected 2961.03377700389, got 2961.033777003901636716262779605767 (2961.0337770039 at the 15 significant digits recorded) |

**None of these is a defect in this runtime.** Every one is the same
`(1 + r/12) ** -n` payment formula, and for each the value produced here is
identical to Apache KIE Drools 10.2.0 across all 34 significant digits —
and both agree with the mathematically exact result. The TCK's recorded
expectation was computed at lower precision and matches neither engine.
The arithmetic is analysed in [unverified semantics](unverified-semantics.md).

They stay in the baseline as failures because they *are* failures against
the TCK as written, and inventing a category to excuse them would be
grading our own homework. Against any engine that agrees with the
reference implementation, level 2 is clean.

## Why the remaining assertions fail

Grouped by cause rather than by category label, because the category says
what happened and the cause says what is missing.

| Theme | Assertions | Share of all failures |
|---|---:|---:|
| Built-in function library | 413 | 37.4% |
| Produced a value, and it was wrong | 242 | 21.9% |
| Unary-test forms | 158 | 14.3% |
| Type checking with `instance of` | 106 | 9.6% |
| Iteration and filters | 85 | 7.7% |
| TCK expected an error, we produced a value | 58 | 5.3% |
| Excluded by design | 21 | 1.9% |
| Named parameters in invocation | 13 | 1.2% |
| Other unsupported constructs | 6 | 0.5% |
| Boxed expression forms | 2 | 0.2% |

**Excluded by design** is not work in progress. FEEL `external` bindings name
host code for the engine to execute, which this runtime refuses to do
([SECURITY.md](../SECURITY.md)). Those assertions will never pass here,
and counting them as failures rather than quietly filtering them out is the
honest presentation.

## Reproducing this

```bash
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/dmn-tck/tck.git vendor/tck
```

```bash
npm run tck
```

`npm run tck` asserts the committed baseline **exactly** — an unexpected pass
fails the build just as an unexpected failure does, because a test that starts
passing usually means it was misclassified. `npm run tck -- --report <CATEGORY>`
lists the individual assertions behind any row above, and
[`tck-baseline.json`](../packages/tck-runner/tck-baseline.json) itemises every
one of them.

`npm run diff` puts this runtime, Drools 10.2.0 and the TCK expectation side by
side, so a divergence says not just *that* two engines disagree but *which one
the TCK backs* — see [differential testing](differential-testing.md).

## Submission

These results are self-measured and have not been submitted to the DMN TCK
for publication. They will be once compliance level 2 is clean and every
remaining level 3 failure has a documented cause — not before.
